songs.name: Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) Jam

ai_show_review.summary: 31‑min Midnight Hour marathon, epic Viola Lee Blues, raw ’67 energy
ai_show_review.blurb: The set bursts with a massive 31‑minute “In The Midnight Hour” jam and an organ‑driven “Viola Lee Blues”. Jerry’s soaring guitar and Pigpen’s powerful organ dominate, while “Alligator” adds another high‑water mark. Overall the performance offers a raw glimpse of the Dead’s emerging psychedelic direction.
ai_show_review.review: On September 3, 1967 at Rio Nido’s Dance Hall the Grateful Dead delivered a blistering, jam‑heavy set that foreshadows their later Dark Star explorations. The show opens with “Dancin’ In The Street,” which, while uneven, hints at early psychedelic improvisation before giving way to a monumental 31‑minute rendition of “In The Midnight Hour” where Jerry Garcia’s guitar soars in transcendent leads. Pigpen’s organ takes center stage on the sprawling “Viola Lee Blues,” weaving soulful textures that drive the band’s exploratory flow, and his presence shines again on “Alligator.” Throughout the night the rhythm section underpins the extended jams with a raw, energetic feel that captures the band at a pivotal moment of evolution.

best_recording.reason: Decent soundboard tape with clear capture of the legendary Midnight Hour jam and overall good balance despite minor hiss.

key_highlights: 31‑minute “In The Midnight Hour” marathon that showcases Garcia’s soaring leads.
Expansive, organ‑driven “Viola Lee Blues” featuring Pigpen’s standout solos.
Powerful “Alligator” performance hinting at the band’s psychedelic future.
Early Dark Star improvisational threads emerging during “Dancin’ In The Street.”

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers transcendent, soaring guitar work throughout, especially on the marathon Midnight Hour and the extended Viola Lee Blues jams.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh’s bass underpins the sprawling improvisations with a solid, supportive foundation.
band_performance.Bob: Weir provides prominent rhythm and vocal contributions, though his playing on Dancin’ In The Street is noted as less focused.
band_performance.Brent: Ron "Pigpen" McKernan’s organ drives the Viola Lee Blues and adds power to Alligator, delivering standout organ solos.
